 Federal Board of Revenue FBR to Launch New Online Tax Refund System by December
 Web Desk November 18, 2026 November 18, 2026 3 min read 
 The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) is set to introduce a new online tax refund system by December 2026 to accelerate the processing of exporters’ pending refund claims, improve transparency and address long-standing delays in tax refunds.
 FBR Chairman Rashid Mahmood Langrial announced the initiative while addressing the business community at the Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI) on Tuesday. He said the new digital system would allow exporters to submit required documents online and receive decisions on their pending refund claims within specified timelines.
 The development is expected to provide relief to exporters facing cash-flow difficulties due to delays in the settlement of tax refunds. Langrial also revealed that tax refunds issued during the current year had increased by 30% compared with the previous year.
 In another major announcement, the FBR chairman said a dedicated online hearing facility for customs valuation cases would become operational in Lahore. The facility will enable local importers to attend hearings and pursue valuation disputes without travelling to Karachi, reducing administrative costs and inconvenience.
 Langrial further stated that the FBR would consider expanding the powers of the Director of Customs Valuation Lahore to improve the resolution of valuation-related disputes. Complaints regarding incorrect customs valuation rates and alleged irregularities would be examined through daily hearings conducted by a senior officer.
 He assured the business community that responsibility would be determined wherever wrongdoing was established and that the Lahore Chamber would be kept informed about the action taken on complaints.
 The FBR chairman also discussed government initiatives aimed at supporting small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and said the tax authority was willing to review traders’ concerns and proposals regarding the fixed tax scheme.
 During the meeting, LCCI President Ali Hussam Asghar urged the government to introduce business-friendly tax policies that promote investment, industrial expansion and employment rather than focusing exclusively on revenue collection.
 He proposed a special incentive-based tax scheme for SME exporters and a one-time tax exemption for industries investing in balancing, modernisation and replacement (BMR) of machinery and production facilities.
 Highlighting the challenges faced by Pakistani exporters, Asghar said local businesses were operating with an estimated 8% to 10% cost disadvantage compared with regional competitors. He called for targeted tax incentives for export-oriented industries and proposed reducing advance tax on exporters from 2% to 1%.
 The LCCI president also raised concerns over delayed customs procedures and the prolonged blockage of importers’ funds, calling for a joint committee comprising representatives of the FBR and LCCI to resolve business-related tax and customs issues.
 Regarding customs valuation disputes, he reiterated the need to strengthen the Lahore Directorate of Customs Valuation and introduce online hearings through Zoom so importers could present their cases without unnecessary travel.
 To improve coordination between the business community and tax authorities, Asghar designated LCCI Secretary General Shahid Khalil as the chamber’s focal person for FBR-related matters.
 Senior FBR officials, including Member Customs Syed Shakeel Shah and Chief Collector Appraisement Lahore Naveed Elahi, also attended the meeting along with LCCI office-bearers and representatives of the business community.
 The proposed online refund system marks another step towards digitalisation of tax administration in Pakistan, with exporters expecting faster refund settlements, improved cash flows and greater transparency in the processing of their legitimate tax refund claims.
